contract.instance: Unweighted complete signed graph; every unordered vertex pair is positive or negative.
contract.encoding: An ordinary graph G=(V,E) contains exactly the positive pairs; nonedges represent negative pairs.
contract.objective: Number of positive edges crossing clusters plus number of negative pairs inside clusters.
contract.output: A partition into any number of clusters; each vertex learns its own cluster ID.
contract.communicationGraph: The positive-edge graph G itself, not the complete signed graph and not an arbitrary external network.
contract.model: Synchronous LOCAL: one computationally unbounded processor per vertex; communication with neighbors in G.
contract.messageSize: The implementation uses O(log n)-bit messages, so its bandwidth also fits CONGEST.
contract.guaranteeType: Expected objective approximation, not a claimed high-probability approximation ratio.

theorems.sourceLocation: Corollary 1.5, printed p. 4; proof in Section 4, printed pp. 25–26
theorems.statement: For any epsilon > 0, there is a randomized O(1/epsilon)-round LOCAL algorithm for a (3+epsilon)-approximation using O(log n)-bit messages.
theorems.interpretation: Expected approximation; this expectation is explicit in the implementation theorem and follows from Corollary 1.2 / Claim 4.1.
theorems.epsilonScope: The source states any epsilon > 0. A displayed interval such as 0 < epsilon <= 1 would be a plotting restriction, not a theorem restriction.

theorems.equivalentRoundExpression: E[COST] <= (3 + 8/(T-2) + n^{-Omega(1)}) OPT for odd integer T >= 3
theorems.implementation: Each of r Pivot phases uses two communication rounds; one final round assigns clusters.
theorems.randomness: Vertices independently choose ranks uniformly from {0,...,n^c-1}, for sufficiently large constant c, with rank ties broken by vertex ID.
theorems.finiteRankCaution: Do not advertise an exact 3+epsilon guarantee at r=ceil(4/epsilon+1/2) while dropping the rank-collision correction.

theorems.expectedCorrectionUpperBoundFromProof: n^{4-c}, written n^{-Omega(1)} for sufficiently large constant c
theorems.exactZeroOptHandling: If every connected component is a clique, both variants recover the optimum with probability 1. Otherwise OPT >= 1, allowing the collision-event cost to be bounded relative to OPT.
theorems.caution: High probability that ranks are distinct does not turn the expected approximation theorem into a high-probability approximation theorem.

theorems.statement: With a globally uniform random permutation, r-Pivot has expected approximation at most 3+8/(2r-1).
theorems.caveat: The LOCAL implementation uses independently generated finite ranks and therefore includes the additional vanishing correction.

lowerBoundAudit.mainFigureNote: No general LOCAL round lower bound is proved in the supplied source.

representationProposal.recommended: Discrete expected-approximation versus elapsed-round tradeoff family.
representationProposal.approximationAxis: Expected approximation upper guarantee; equivalently epsilon above 3.
representationProposal.lowerBoundColor: red reserved for actual verified lower bounds; none supplied here
representationProposal.approximationThreeReference: Neutral reference only, explicitly not a hardness bound.
representationProposal.correctionDisplay: Keep +n^{-Omega(1)} explicit in caption/inspection; if the base curve 3+8/(T-2) is drawn, label it as the main term plus vanishing rank correction.
representationProposal.noNumericSubstitution: Do not assign a numerical exponent to Omega(1) or silently evaluate the correction.
representationProposal.fullAtlas: Retain the green tradeoff and concise labels '(3+epsilon) expected' and 'O(1/epsilon) rounds'; hide theorem detail at distant zoom.
representationProposal.meaningfulClarification: Should the figure show how rounds grow as expected approximation approaches 3, or fix an approximation target such as 3.1?

additionalTheorems.theorem: Fischer–Noever Theorem 1.1 together with the standard Pivot reduction; BCMT22 Table 1 and Section 1.1 explicitly record the LOCAL factor-3 consequence
additionalTheorems.graph: Unweighted complete signed graph encoded by its positive-edge graph; nonedges are negative pairs

additionalTheorems.guarantee: E[cost] ≤ 3 OPT; O(log n) rounds with high probability
additionalTheorems.probability: Expected approximation; round complexity holds with probability at least 1−1/n^c for any fixed c≥2. These are distinct probability statements.
additionalTheorems.derivation: Full parallel Pivot reproduces sequential Pivot. Its expected factor 3 is outside the logarithmic a−3 axis, so it has a separate endpoint card. The Ω(log n) greedy-procedure lower bound is not a lower bound for all correlation-clustering algorithms. This record does not replace the finite-rank correction retained for BCMT22.

Expected cost and high-probability elapsed rounds are separate guarantees

additionalTheorems.theorem: Algorithm 1, Lemma 3.3, and Theorem 3.9; explicit β=λ=1/36 in the proof; LOCAL round implementation derived here
additionalTheorems.graph: Unweighted complete signed graph encoded by positive edges; missing pairs are negative
additionalTheorems.resource: LOCAL on the positive-edge graph; exchanging whole neighbor lists requires unrestricted messages
additionalTheorems.guarantee: cost ≤ 1442 OPT; at most 6 communication rounds when neighbor IDs are initially known
additionalTheorems.probability: Deterministic; exact neighborhood comparisons, without MPC sampling
additionalTheorems.derivation: Derivation: one round exchanges closed neighborhoods and determines agreement; one exchanges heavy/light flags; four rounds propagate the maximum ID in each trimmed component (diameter at most four by Lemma 3.3). Six rounds suffice with known neighbor IDs; allow one additional initial ID exchange otherwise. Theorem 3.9 explicitly certifies 1442 for these parameters. We do not use approximately optimized 701 as an exact bound. This is not the randomized MPC implementation and is not claimed to use CONGEST bandwidth.
assumptions: No restriction on LOCAL message size

additionalTheorems.theorem: Theorem 12; correlation-clustering discussion at the end of Section 3.3
additionalTheorems.graph: General weighted signed graphs; missing edges contribute no agreement weight
additionalTheorems.resource: CONGEST on the signed input network, with O(log n)-bit messages; also a LOCAL algorithm
additionalTheorems.guarantee: Agreement weight ≥ (1/2−ε) OPT; O(log* n) rounds for fixed ε>0
additionalTheorems.derivation: The theorem states O(log* n) with ε fixed; the display does not assert that the hidden constant is independent of ε. This maximization guarantee cannot be converted to a multiplicative minimum-disagreement guarantee. All vertices choose from two cluster labels.

additionalTheorems.graph: Unweighted signed network excluding a fixed minor H; missing edges have no objective term
additionalTheorems.resource: CONGEST on the signed H-minor-free input network; unrestricted local computation may solve cluster subproblems exactly
additionalTheorems.guarantee: Agreements ≥ (1−ε) OPT in ε^{−O(1)} log^{O(1)} n rounds with high probability
additionalTheorems.derivation: Separate from weighted general graphs and complete-signed minimum-disagreement instances. The proof gathers each component and computes an optimal clustering locally; local computational work is not bounded polynomially. Round exponents are independent of H, while constants may depend on H. Footnote 1 also notes a general-graph LOCAL (1−ε) approximation via low-diameter decomposition; we do not promote that brief observation to an additional fully audited theorem.
assumptions: Maximize agreements on signed network edges
Potentially expensive local computation is allowed
